title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines conventions, templates, and operating procedures for all Developer Experience (DX) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues plus their fixes. The goal is to ensure consistent, reliable, discoverable documentation that reduces time-to-value for engineers and minimizes repetitive support burden.

Scope

- Content types: SDK guides, language quickstarts, API example recipes, reference docs, docs-site runbook and publishing procedures, troubleshooting KB (support-top-issues).
- Audience: software engineers, ML engineers, platform engineers, solutions engineers, customer support.
- Ownership model: Authors write content; reviewers from Product/Platform validate accuracy; Docs maintainers publish and operate docs site.

Documentation Principles

1. Accuracy first: docs must match shipped behavior. Prefer short code examples that run (curl, Python, JS).
2. Reproducibility: include copy-paste commands and exact dependency versions for quickstarts.
3. Discoverability: use clear titles, short descriptions, and tags.
4. Maintainability: include a short checklist for updates and automated tests where feasible.
5. Support-first: every quickstart must include a troubleshooting section with 3–5 canonical fixes.

Document Types and Minimum Content

- SDK Guide (per-language):
  - Short intro and platform fit (100–200 words).
  - Installation commands and supported versions.
  - Minimal complete example (init, request, handle streaming/errors).
  - Advanced topics: batching, retries, configuration for Dedicated/Private.
  - Compatibility table: runtime versions, authentication patterns.
  - Troubleshooting (top 5 issues).

- Quickstart / Template:
  - Goal and estimated completion time.
  - Prereqs (account, API key, region).
  - Step-by-step numbered instructions with runnable commands.
  - Template repo link (if applicable) and deploy notes.
  - Tests: smoke test command and expected output.

- API Examples: short, focused recipes (curl, Python, JS) covering generation, chat, embeddings, function calling, streaming. Each example must include expected response snippets and notes about token limits, model selection, and performance tips.

- Docs Site Operating Procedures: publishing flow, rollback, CI linting, analytics, and incident response for broken pages.

- Support Top Issues KB: canonical diagnostic steps and safe fixes that support and SEs can perform or escalate.

Templates and Examples

1) Minimal SDK guide header (example)

Title: Redwood Python SDK: Quickstart
Summary: Install and call the Redwood API from Python for text generation.
Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip, Redwood API key.

Install:
```
python -m pip install --upgrade redwood-inference
```

Minimal example (Python):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate("Write a 50-word product description for a developer platform.")
print(resp.text)
```

Notes:
- Use CLIENT.stream() for low-latency character-level streaming.
- For Dedicated customers, set region and pool_id in client config.

2) Quickstart checklist (publish-ready)

- Title and 1-line summary
- Prereqs (include links to signup and API key docs)
- 3–6 numbered steps with commands
- Smoke-test command + expected output
- Troubleshooting section (3 canonical issues)
- Tested on the docs CI against the latest SDK release

Publishing and Review Process (Docs Site Runbook)

1. Author creates draft in confluence with the standard template and tags (labels).
2. Assign two reviewers: one from Product/Applied ML (accuracy) and one from Eng Platform (operational).
3. Run docs CI: linting, link-check, code-block execution (where supported).
4. After approvals, move status to published and add page to appropriate navigation category.
5. Update changelog entry in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/change-log (date, author, summary).
6. Post-publication smoke test: run the guide's smoke-test and record result.

Rollback procedure:

- If a page introduces incorrect technical guidance, set status to draft and append an "errata" notice at the top pointing to the safe alternative. Notify the docs-maintainers Slack channel and the reviewers. Restore the previous version using the Confluence page history.

Docs CI and Automated Checks

- Lint: prose style checks (no passive voice in short instructions), required sections present.
- Link-check: fail on 404s for internal links.
- Snippet execution: run Python/JS smoke tests in ephemeral containers; fail publish if smoke-test fails.
- Size and performance: pages > 200KB flagged for asset optimization.

Canonical Support Issues and Fixes (Top 10)

Each entry below includes: symptom, quick diagnostic, canonical fix, escalation criteria.

1) API 401 / Invalid API key
- Symptom: 401 responses for all requests.
- Diagnostic: confirm X-API-Key header present, check key prefix, ensure key is not expired via console.
- Fix: rotate key in account console and update environment variables; restart long-lived worker.
- Escalate if key appears active but service returns 401 -> escalate to Auth team with request_id and timestamp.

2) High latency for streaming responses
- Symptom: streaming emits in large chunks or stalls.
- Diagnostic: check client SDK version, network latency, model selection, and server-side logs for batching delays.
- Fix: upgrade SDK to latest streaming patch; enable chunked transfer encoding in proxy; for Dedicated, pin to low-latency pool.

3) Token limit / 413 Request Entity Too Large
- Symptom: requests with long prompts get rejected.
- Diagnostic: confirm model max context length and total tokens (prompt + completion).
- Fix: paginate long documents using embeddings + retrieval, truncate boilerplate, or use a longer-context model.

4) Mismatch between example code and SDK behavior
- Symptom: example in docs causes runtime error.
- Diagnostic: check pinned SDK version in code sample vs latest API.
- Fix: update sample to include explicit versioned import or add a compatibility note; add CI test that runs sample.

5) Explanation of rate limit 429 errors
- Symptom: 429 during bursts.
- Diagnostic: check headers x-rw-limit and usage metrics, identify route and quota.
- Fix: implement exponential backoff with jitter; suggest client-side token-bucket for high-throughput use; advise on Dedicated capacity options.

6) Private deployment auth failures
- Symptom: Private (VPC) customers receive 403 from control plane or errors during KMS usage.
- Diagnostic: verify VPC peering, firewall rules, and KMS grants.
- Fix: run the provided network diagnostics script and confirm KMS key policy; coordinate with eng-private-deployments on trace.

7) Broken code snippet due to library deprecation
- Symptom: snippet raises DeprecationError.
- Diagnostic: run snippet CI and produce stacktrace.
- Fix: update snippet, add note about minimal supported versions, and add to docs CI failing tests.

8) Streaming disconnects when behind corporate proxy
- Symptom: streaming drops midway; connection reset.
- Diagnostic: confirm proxy supports upgrade and long-lived connections.
- Fix: recommend WebSocket-based streaming or configure proxy to allow chunked responses and longer timeouts.

9) Embeddings mismatch across SDKs
- Symptom: embeddings vectors differ more than expected between Python and JS SDKs.
- Diagnostic: verify model and tokenizer versions, check float vs quantized encoding.
- Fix: add note that embeddings must use identical model and tokenizer; include checksum test in SDK guides.

10) Confusing example around function-calling
- Symptom: function call example produces unexpected JSON schema errors.
- Diagnostic: validate schema against the example payload and check SDK's function-calling wrapper.
- Fix: expand example to show strict schema validation, include validation helper, and link to the model serving standards ADR.

Ownership and SLAs for Docs Issues

- First responder: Docs triage engineer (owned by engineering) - SLA: acknowledge within 2 business days.
- Technical reviewer (Product/Platform): respond with proposed fix within 5 business days for non-critical issues.
- Critical errors (security, billing, or safety): 24-hour remediation target and page errata posted immediately.

Metrics and KPIs

- Page health (link failures, outdated code samples) < 2% per quarter.
- Average time to first fix (docs bugs) < 7 days.
- Reduction in duplicate support tickets referencing docs by 30% YOY.

Appendix: Quick Publishing Checklist

- [ ] Title, one-line summary, and tags present
- [ ] Prereqs and smoke-test included
- [ ] Code examples verified by CI
- [ ] Reviewers assigned and approvals recorded
- [ ] Navigation and related_pages updated
- [ ] Changelog entry added

Contact and ownership

- Docs maintainers: docs@redwood.ai (primary inbox)
- Slack channel: #docs-maintainers
- Page owner: Asha Patel (author)

Related pages

- SDK Guides index: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides
- Quickstarts and templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Support top issues: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues

End of playbook. For questions or suggested edits, please create a pull request in the docs repo and tag the docs-maintainers group.
